(a) Qualifications.—Effective as of the date of the enactment of this Act, no individual may be selected to serve in the position of Regional Director under the TRICARE program unless the indi- vidual—
        (1) is—
            (A) an officer of the Armed Forces in a general or flag officer grade;  
            (B) a civilian employee of the Department of Defense in the Senior Executive Service; or 
            (C) a civilian employee of the Federal Government in a department or agency other than the Department of Defense, or a civilian working in the private sector, who has experience in a position comparable to an officer described in subparagraph (A) or a civilian employee described in subparagraph (B); and  
        (2) has at least 10 years of experience, or equivalent expertise or training, in the military health care system, managed care, and health care policy and administration.  
    (b) Tricare Program Defined.—In this section, the term “TRICARE program” has the meaning given such term in section 1072(7) of title 10, United States Code.

fable.w: The section only sets eligibility qualifications for a federal position, TRICARE Regional Director. The tempting reading is that the reference to "a civilian working in the private sector" brings in outsiders, but that person would be hired as a federal official, not consulted on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.

opus.w: This section only sets eligibility rules for appointment to a federal position, the TRICARE Regional Director. Mentioning private-sector civilians may look like outside involvement, but they appear only as possible appointees, and once selected they would be federal officials doing their jobs, not outsiders advising on a decision. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue is created.
opus.s: a civilian working in the private sector, who has experience in a position comparable to an officer described in subparagraph (A) or a civilian employee described in subparagraph (B)
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that the phrase "a civilian working in the private sector" brings an outside party into a federal decision. That reading fails. This section only sets the qualifications someone needs to be appointed TRICARE Regional Director. A private-sector person who is selected becomes a federal official doing the job. As in Example 7, government employees doing their jobs are not participating. Nothing here requires or allows the government to consult outside parties, hold a hearing, take public comment, form an advisory body or let anyone sue before it decides something.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section sets hiring qualifications for a federal position (Regional Director). Although it allows hiring from the private sector, the individual becomes a federal employee/official upon appointment. The definition excludes internal government actors and employees from 'participation.' There is no requirement for consultation with outside entities, public comment, or advisory boards composed of non-federal members.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Qualifications.—Effective as of the date of the enactment of this Act, no individual may be selected to serve in the position of Regional Director under the TRICARE program unless the indi- vidual— (1) is— (A) an officer of the Armed Forces in a general or flag officer grade; (B) a civilian employee of the Department of Defense in the Senior Executive Service; or (C) a civilian employee of the Federal Government in a department or agency other than the Department of Defense, or a civilian working in the private sector, who has experience in a position comparable to an officer described in subparagraph (A) or a civilian employee described in subparagraph (B); and (2) has at least 10 years of experience, or equivalent expertise or training, in the military health care system, managed care, and health care policy and administration.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allowing a "civilian working in the private sector" to serve as a Regional Director constitutes participation because it involves an outsider in a government role. However, the definition explicitly states that federal employees and officials are inside the government, and serving in a federal position (even if hired from the private sector) makes one a federal employee/official, not an outside participant in the decision-making process. The section describes hiring qualifications for internal agency staff, not a mechanism for external consultation or advisory input.
